question: A bus travelling at 75 km/hr completes a journey in 17 hours. What should be its speed to cover the same distance in 5 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional.

S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂

⇒ 75 × 17 = S₂ × 5

⇒ S₂ = (75 × 17) ÷ 5

⇒ S₂ = 15 × 17 = 255 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 255 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 Total Distance (D) is Constant
 
 
 Case 1: Speed = 75 km/hr | Time = 17 hrs
 
 
 Case 2: Speed = ? | Time = 5 hrs
 
 
• 
 
• 

**Given:**

Initial Speed (S₁) = 75 km/hr

Initial Time (T₁) = 17 hours

New Time (T₂) = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Distance = 75 × 17

⇒ Total Distance = 1275 km

Now, to cover the same distance in 5 hours:

⇒ New Speed (S₂) = Total Distance ÷ New Time

⇒ S₂ = 1275 ÷ 5

⇒ S₂ = 255 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 255 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality Rule

If Distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional (S ∝ 1 / T). Therefore, the ratio of speeds is the inverse of the ratio of times taken.

Average Speed

When traveling equal distances at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed is given by (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, it is |S₁ − S₂|.
